title: Karnataka Campaign and Deccani Alliance
subtitle: Shivaji’s March to the Southern Horizon
region: Hyderabad, Golconda, Vellore, Gingee, Mysore plateau and Thanjavur
moral: Wise strategy chooses allies by purpose, not by labels.

sources.citation: Sabhasad Bakhar, tr. S.N. Sen, southern campaign, Vellore, Gingee and Venkoji settlement
sources.note: Most detailed Maratha narrative for the expedition.

sources.citation: EIC Madras Factory Records, 1677, India Office Records, British Library
sources.note: Contemporary English monitoring of Shivaji's southern movements.

sources.citation: G.S. Sardesai, New History of the Marathas, Vol. 1, pp. 240-265
sources.note: Classic synthesis of Maratha, Golconda and British evidence.

sources.citation: Gijs Kruijtzer, Xenophobia in Seventeenth-Century India, Leiden University Press, 2009, ch. 5
sources.note: Useful for the rhetoric of Deccani solidarity and later communalization debates.

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of an army on the move across the Deccan plateau

dialogue.text: In 1677, Shivaji, Hindu king of the west, joined hands with Abu Hasan, Muslim sultan of Golconda, and marched south—not for faith, but for the future of the Deccan.

panels.shot: slow push-in on Shivaji over a campaign map lit by oil lamps

dialogue.text: By the late 1670s, the Mughal tide pressed from the north, Bijapur still watched from the east, and Shivaji’s gaze turned beyond the Ghats to the rich plains of Karnataka.

panels.shot: medium close-up on Shivaji’s thoughtful face, profile lit against darkness

dialogue.text: There, south of the Tungabhadra, lay old jagirs of Shahaji, his father; there too lay the line of Venkoji, his half-brother, and the shadow of Bijapur’s broken but lingering power.

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of the Deccan showing three powers in different colors

dialogue.text: To stand against the Mughal-Bijapur squeeze, Shivaji needed depth—new strongholds, fresh revenues, allies who feared imperial overreach as much as he did.

panels.shot: courtly mid-shot of Shivaji dictating a letter to a scribe

dialogue.text: So letters rode out from Raigad to Hyderabad, to Abu Hasan Qutb Shah of Golconda—a Persianate court, Shia Muslim, but a Deccani kingdom wary of Aurangzeb’s hunger.

panels.shot: opulent interior wide of the Golconda court

dialogue.text: Golconda’s rulers had long balanced Mughal threats with alliances. An offer from a rising Maratha king promised a new axis of defense across the Deccan.

panels.shot: medium shot on Abu Hasan in deliberation with advisors

dialogue.text: Abu Hasan weighed the risks; but the Mughals menaced his northern frontiers, and Bijapur’s decline stirred old ambitions. A pact with Shivaji could carve a shared buffer in the south.

panels.shot: dramatic wide of a field camp where envoys meet

dialogue.text: The alliance that followed was practical and clear: Golconda subsidies and passage, Maratha arms in the field, shared gains in the Karnataka where Bijapur and local chiefs still held sway.

panels.shot: wide tracking shot of the Maratha army entering Golconda-held territory

dialogue.text: English factors from distant Madras recorded the march with cold curiosity: a western Hindu king moving under a Muslim sultan’s sanction, toward the Tamil and Kannada lands.

panels.shot: dynamic mid-wide of Maratha troops crossing a river

dialogue.text: This was not a raid but a campaign. Grain trains, siege guns, locally hired guides and interpreters moved with the host, knitting Maharashtra to the far south with dusty roads and shared danger.

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Vellore fort in the distance

dialogue.text: Targets were chosen with care. Forts like Vellore controlled passes, trade and armies. Each stronghold taken would be a knot binding Maratha influence to the southern plains.

panels.shot: medium shot of Shivaji consulting a local ally outside Vellore

dialogue.text: Here, too, statecraft moved ahead of steel. Some commanders bargained, some defected, some weighed which side would better guard their income and their shrines.

panels.shot: wide shot of Gingee fort looming over rugged hills

dialogue.text: Further east stood Gingee, its triple hills and deep defenses famed in the south. To control it was to command a citadel that could outlast storms of war.

panels.shot: mid-shot of Shivaji pointing toward Gingee with his sword

dialogue.speaker: chhatrapati_shivaji_maharaj
dialogue.text: A fort like this is a promise: for us, or against us.

panels.shot: medium close-up of Shivaji in a council tent

dialogue.text: Sabhasad later recounted the steady succession of sieges and submissions. Not every gate needed battering; some opened for timely payment, some for fear of future Mughal wrath.

panels.shot: wide of a local temple town with Maratha and local soldiers mingling

dialogue.text: As forts fell, towns adjusted. Marathi commands and Kannada or Tamil tongues mingled in markets and shrines, as new garrisons promised order, tax collection and protection from distant emperors.

panels.shot: tense mid-shot of Shivaji receiving news about Mysore

dialogue.text: Yet the land was not empty. Mysore’s Wodeyar ruler and other chiefs watched this new power from the west. Some resisted, some bargained, judging whether Maratha rule would be lighter than old overlords.

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot of Shivaji reading a letter by lamplight

dialogue.text: For Shivaji, Karnataka was not foreign soil. His father Shahaji had served and held jagirs here under Bijapur. To him, this march also reclaimed a family claim and secured distant kin.

panels.shot: dramatic two-shot of Shivaji confronting Venkoji in a hall

dialogue.text: Most delicate of all was Venkoji of Thanjavur, Shahaji’s younger son. Between them lay shared blood, old rights in the south, and the question of who would rule which lands.

panels.shot: medium close-up alternating between Shivaji and Venkoji

dialogue.speaker: chhatrapati_shivaji_maharaj
dialogue.text: Let our father’s house not weaken itself while others circle these lands.

panels.shot: wide shot of scribes and officials drafting a settlement

dialogue.text: Through days of talk came settlement: obligations for Venkoji to pay, territories to acknowledge, a recognition that Shivaji’s sway now reached into the Thanjavur orbit, though Venkoji kept his throne.

panels.shot: wide of the coastline near Madras with distant European ships

dialogue.text: From Madras, English factors wrote of these shifts with unease. New powers in Vellore and Gingee could threaten trade routes, or be bargained with against rivals.

panels.shot: medium shot of Shivaji in prayer or quiet reflection before departure

dialogue.text: By year’s end, a chain of forts, revenues and understandings tied Maharashtra to the south. Shivaji had not planted a new capital here, but he had planted options.

panels.shot: heroic low-angle wide of Shivaji’s army beginning its return north

dialogue.text: Later, Rajaram would use Gingee as a refuge against Mughal storms. That future was possible because this campaign had laid foundations far beyond the Sahyadris.

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Shivaji’s steady eyes, fading into maps and flags

dialogue.text: In an age later sliced into religious lines, this march tells another truth: Shivaji chose allies and foes by power and purpose, not by creed—a lesson in politics that still unsettles easy tales.
